# ── Concurrency ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

## 12. Database column reference

*Embedded from `DATABASE_COLUMNS.md` — kept as a separate file because it is rendered live by the Developer page (Schema tab). Edit the source file, not this section.*

##### EETRA Material Library — Database Column Reference

This document describes the **content and purpose of each column** in the Material Library database. The data is sourced from the Excel file **EETRA_MaterialLibrary.xlsx** (sheet: `_live_data`), and may also be loaded from SharePoint, local Parquet, or MotherDuck. Column names use a **prefix** (e.g. `A__`, `D__`, `P__`) to group fields by category.

---

###### Column naming convention

- **Format:** `PREFIX__FieldName` (e.g. `A__ProductName`, `G__GWP_A1A3`).
- **Prefixes** group columns for display (e.g. Details, Properties, EPD Info, GWP Data, Recycling, VOC).
- In the app, prefixes can be stripped for cleaner labels (e.g. `G__GWP_A1A3` → `GWP_A1A3`).
- The `0__` prefix marks record identifiers; single-underscore variants (`V_Test_Standard`, `V_Report_Type`, `V_CAM_Compliance`) also exist for a few VOC/CAM fields.

---

###### 0 — Record identifiers

| Column | Purpose | Content / notes |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **0__EETRA_ID** | Product key | Strict `TYPE__SUBTYPE__NNNN` identifier (e.g. `INS__FIB__0494`). Primary key for tags, collections, media file naming, and the Add/Edit Item page. |
| **0__NUM** | Sequence number | Numeric row sequence used for ordering; auto-incremented when new items are added. |

---

###### A — Product identity & attributes

| Column | Purpose | Content / notes |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **A__Manufacturer** | Manufacturer or brand name | Company name (e.g. Knauf, Gyproc). Used for filters, catalogue, charts, maps, and manufacturer logos. |
| **A__ProductName** | Commercial product name | Full product name as in catalogues. Used for sorting, cards, and as primary label in charts/maps. |
| **A__ProductDescription** | Product description | Free-text description / marketing summary of the product. |
| **A__ProductName_Base** | Base product (derived) | Normalized product name used for grouping variants (e.g. thickness). Populated by app logic from `A__ProductName`. |
| **A__Map_yn** | Include in map view | `Y` = show on maps; other/missing = exclude. Used to filter rows in MAPS tab and Developer "Tabular Data". |
| **A__Thickness_mm** | Thickness (attribute) | Thickness in mm when stored at product level (alternative to property thickness). |

---

###### B — Board / block attributes

| Column | Purpose | Content / notes |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **B__Thickness_mm** | Board/block thickness | Thickness in mm for board/block products. Used in fallback chains for display (with `P__Thick_mm`, `E__EPD_Thick_mm`, etc.). |

---

###### D — Details (product type, material, technical)

| Column | Purpose | Content / notes |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **D__ProductType_ENG** | Product type (English) | High-level type (e.g. Insulation, Building boards, Binder, In situ Concrete). Drives filter options and field visibility per product type. |
| **D__MaterialType_ENG** | Material type (English) | More specific material classification. Used in sidebar filters and tabular visibility. |
| **D__MaterialType_ITA** | Material type (Italian) | Italian-language material classification (localisation of `D__MaterialType_ENG`). |
| **D__Size** | Size / dimensions | Product size or dimensional description (free text). |

###### PR — List prices (runtime-derived)

These columns are **not** in the source Excel and are **not** stored in any
dataset parquet. `app.py` attaches them to `ORIGINAL_DATA` on load via
`libs/lib_prices.py` `fn507_attach_prices`, joining the catalogue to
`01_data/price_lists.parquet` on manufacturer + normalised product name +
thickness. Because they are derived, they never enter `edits_data.parquet` and
are excluded from the Developer missing-data matrix (its prefix rule is a single
letter).

The prices themselves are **list prices** (listino, VAT excluded, before any
discount), read from the manufacturers' published PDF listini by
`04_tools/13_parse_price_lists.py` (first source: URSA Italia, 9 listini,
331 priced SKUs + 15 accessories/surcharges in `01_data/price_supplements.parquet`).
They are an indication for design comparison, never a quotation — the UI always
shows the listino edition next to the figure.

Clicking the price on a card opens the manufacturer's **full listino table** for
that product (`fn511_price_table_for_product` / `fn512_price_tables_payload`,
injected as `window.__PRICE_TABLES__`): every SKU with code, size, price,
availability and packaging, exactly as printed. That is what a catalogue entry
covering a thickness *range* (e.g. `Glasswool DF 39`, 50–240 mm) expands into —
the twelve thicknesses actually sold. For an entry naming a single thickness the
matching row is highlighted instead.

| Column | Purpose | Content / notes |
|--------|---------|------------------|
| **PR__Price_EUR** | List price (SKU) | Price of the matched SKU in its own unit; empty when the catalogue row covers a thickness range rather than one SKU. |
| **PR__Price_EUR_m2** | List price €/m² | Chart axis: only SKU-exact €/m² prices, so a family span never plots as a single product's price. |
| **PR__Cost_per_R** | €/m² per unit R | `PR__Price_EUR_m2 ÷ R`, the cost of a m² per unit of thermal resistance. Offered for Insulation only. |
| **PR__R_m2KW** | Thermal resistance | R (m²K/W) as printed in the listino, else thickness ÷ λ from the listino row. |
| **PR__Price_Min_EUR** / **PR__Price_Max_EUR** | Price span | Cheapest / dearest SKU of the matched product — the range shown for a catalogue row covering several thicknesses. |
| **PR__Price_Unit** | Price basis | `m2`, `m3` or `kg`, per how the manufacturer prices that family. |
| **PR__Price_Exact** | Match quality | `True` when one SKU matched the thickness; `False` when the figure is a family span. |
| **PR__Price_Display** | Display text | Formatted for the UI: `€ 8,05 /m²` or `€ 5,09 – 22,30 /m²`. Feeds the catalogue card row and detail panel. |
| **PR__Listino_Edition** | Listino edition | E.g. `Giugno 2026 (rev. 00/26)` — shown with every price. |
| **PR__Listino_URL** | Listino source | Link to the manufacturer's price-list PDF the figure was read from. |

###### Data source and cleaning

- **Source:** Excel `EETRA_MaterialLibrary.xlsx`, sheet `_live_data` (or equivalent from SharePoint / Parquet / MotherDuck).
- **Cleaning:** Unnamed/empty columns and marker rows (e.g. starting with `*`) are dropped. Data from the Excel is cut at the last expected column (`V__DOP`); the pipeline then appends the helper columns above. Rows with empty product name and manufacturer may be dropped when `A__Map_yn` is used.
- **Visibility:** Which columns appear in catalogue and tabular view depends on **product type** and on `aux_10__ui_config.json` (`field_visibility`, `field_meta`, `tabular_column_visibility`).
- **Conversion pipeline:** `04_tools/03_excel_to_parquet.py` converts the Excel DB to `live_data.parquet`, downloads images / EPD / tech-sheet / VOC-cert documents into `01_data/`, and parses VOC-cert PDFs. See the file manifest in `APP_DOCUMENTATION.md`.

## 13. CAM 2025 — recycled-content targets

*Embedded from `CAM.md` — kept as a separate file because it is rendered live by the CAM 2025 page. Edit the source file, not this section.*

##### CAM 2025 — Target contenuto riciclato (materiali da costruzione)

Fonte: Decreto 24 novembre 2025 (CAM 2025), sintesi operativa per EETRA MatLib.

##### 2.4.7 Isolanti termici e acustici

- Cellulosa: **80%**
- Lana di vetro: **60%**
- Vetro cellulare: **50%**
- Fibre in poliestere: **40%**
- Lana di roccia: **15%**
- Polistirene espanso sinterizzato (EPS, incluse casserature a perdere): **15%** (di cui min. 10% riciclato)
- Polistirene espanso estruso (XPS, incluse casserature a perdere): **10%** (di cui min. 5% riciclato)
- Agglomerato di poliuretano: **70%**
- Agglomerato di gomma: **60%**
- Poliuretano espanso flessibile: **20%**
- Poliuretano espanso rigido: **3% dal 01/01/2026** (di cui min. 2% riciclato)

##### 2.4.8 Tramezzature, contropareti, controsoffitti

- Lastre e pannelli in generale: **10%**
- Lastre in cartongesso e pannelli in gesso: **5%**

##### 2.4.10 Pavimenti resilienti

- Pavimentazioni in materie plastiche: **20%**
- Pavimentazioni in materie plastiche per applicazioni sportive (UNI EN 14904): **5%**
- Pavimentazioni in gomma: **10%**

##### 2.4.12 Serramenti e chiusure oscuranti

- Profili in PVC: **20%**
- Profili in alluminio: **40%**

##### 2.4.6 Prodotti in legno o a base legno

- Pannelli a base legnosa con materiale riciclato: **70%**  
  (certificazione FSC Riciclato o PEFC Riciclato)

##### Assunzione operativa MatLib (catalogazione)

- Piastrelle / ceramici (tiles, gres porcellanato): benchmark operativo **15%** per visualizzazione target CAM nei grafici.

##### Metodi di verifica (esempi)

- EPD (Dichiarazione Ambientale di Prodotto)
- ReMade in Italy
- Plastica Seconda Vita (PSV)
- Certificazione CP DOC 262
- UNI/PdR 88
- Made Green in Italy (MGI)

##### Criterio premiante 2.6.6

- Almeno **15% in peso** di tutti i materiali (esclusi quelli già coperti dal cap. 2.4)
  con contenuto riciclato/recuperato/sottoprodotti.
- Di questo, almeno **5%** deve essere costituito da materiali non strutturali.


## 14. GWP A1–A3 conversion factors

*Embedded from `GWP_CONVERSIONS.md` — kept as a separate file because it is rendered live by the Developer page (App Documentation → GWP conversion factors tab) and the Add/Edit Item GWP Data tab. Edit the source file, not this section.*

### GWP A1–A3 Conversion Factors

How one declared A1–A3 figure becomes four comparable bases — per kg, per m³, per m²
and per m² at R = 1 — which physical inputs each conversion needs, and where the
numbers are produced.

Rendered live in the app at **Developer → 📖 App Documentation → GWP conversion
factors** (that tab adds live row-coverage counts and typeset formulae). The
**➕ Add New Item** and **✏️ Edit Existing Item** forms show the same derivation
applied to the record being edited, at the bottom of the **GWP Data** tab.

All relationships below were validated against `01_data/base_data.parquet`
(1,609 rows): each holds at a median ratio of exactly 1.000 across the rows where
both sides are populated.

---

#### 1. The five GWP bases

Every product carries **one** figure from its EPD — `G__GWP_A1A3`, expressed in the
unit named by `G__GWP_FU`. The `_kg` / `_m3` / `_m2` / `_m2R1` columns are *derived
views* of that same figure, never independent measurements.

| Column | Unit | One unit means | Primary use | Rows populated |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `G__GWP_A1A3` | kg CO₂e / declared unit | The EPD figure exactly as declared, in whatever unit `G__GWP_FU` names. | Card headline, audit trail back to the EPD. | 1,533 / 1,609 |
| `G__GWP_A1A3_kg` | kg CO₂e / kg | Impact of one kilogram of product — a pure material-intensity basis. | Cross-material comparison, Revalu `gwp.a1a3` mapping. | 834 / 1,609 |
| `G__GWP_A1A3_m3` | kg CO₂e / m³ | Impact of one cubic metre of product in place. | Bulk / volumetric products: concrete, blocks, screeds, timber, insulants. | 1,293 / 1,609 |
| `G__GWP_A1A3_m2` | kg CO₂e / m² | Impact of one square metre **at the product's own declared thickness**. | Layered products: boards, tiles, membranes, finishes. | 603 / 1,609 |
| `G__GWP_A1A3_m2R1` | kg CO₂e / m²·(m²K/W) | Impact of the m² of material that delivers a thermal resistance R = 1 m²K/W. | The only functionally fair basis for comparing insulants. | 376 / 1,609 |

*Coverage as of the 2026-09 dataset; the in-app tab recomputes these counts live.*

---

#### 2. Step one — anchor on the declared unit

`G__GWP_FU` states the EPD's declared unit. It decides which normalised column
receives the declared value **unchanged** (or with a pure unit factor). That column
is the anchor; every other basis is then derived from it in step 3.

| `G__GWP_FU` | Anchored column | Factor | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `m3` | `G__GWP_A1A3_m3` | × 1 | Declared per m³ — copied straight across. |
| `m2` | `G__GWP_A1A3_m2` | × 1 | Declared per m² at the stated thickness. |
| `kg` | `G__GWP_A1A3_kg` | × 1 | Declared per kg — copied straight across. |
| `ton` | `G__GWP_A1A3_kg` | × 0.001 | Declared per tonne → divide by 1000. |
| `m2_R1` | `G__GWP_A1A3_m2R1` | × 1 | EPD already declares the R = 1 reference unit. |
| `m` | — | — | Linear declaration (profiles, edgings). No area/volume anchor without a cross-section. |
| `unit` | — | — | Piece-based declaration. Needs pieces per m² or per m³ to normalise. |

Only `ton` carries a non-unity factor: **GWP/kg = GWP/tonne ÷ 1000**. The catalogue
card applies the same rule at display time when no `_kg` value exists
(`libs/lib_ui.py`).

Observed distribution of `G__GWP_FU`: `m3` 768, `m2` 373, `ton` 187, `kg` 115,
`m2_R1` 51, `m` 28, `unit` 7, blank 67.

---

#### 3. Step two — the three physical bridges

Moving between bases needs exactly three material properties: **density**
(mass ↔ volume), **thickness** (volume ↔ area) and **conductivity**
(area ↔ thermal performance).

**Mass ↔ volume — density ρ**

$$\text{GWP}_{kg} = \frac{\text{GWP}_{m^3}}{\rho} \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \text{GWP}_{m^3} = \text{GWP}_{kg} \cdot \rho$$

**Volume ↔ area — thickness d** (stored in mm, used in m)

$$d\,[\mathrm{m}] = \frac{d\,[\mathrm{mm}]}{1000} \qquad \text{GWP}_{m^2} = \text{GWP}_{m^3} \cdot d \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad \text{GWP}_{m^3} = \frac{\text{GWP}_{m^2}}{d}$$

**Area ↔ mass — mass per area m_A**

$$m_A = \rho \cdot d \qquad \text{GWP}_{kg} = \frac{\text{GWP}_{m^2}}{m_A}$$

**Area ↔ thermal performance — conductivity λ**

$$R = \frac{d}{\lambda} \quad\Rightarrow\quad \text{GWP}_{m^2R=1} = \frac{\text{GWP}_{m^2}}{R} = \text{GWP}_{m^2} \cdot \frac{\lambda}{d} = \text{GWP}_{m^3} \cdot \lambda$$

##### Conversion matrix

Read as **row → column**: multiply the row basis by the cell to obtain the column basis.

| from ↓ / to → | per kg | per m³ | per m² | per m² R=1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **per kg** | 1 | × ρ | × ρ·d | × ρ·λ |
| **per m³** | ÷ ρ | 1 | × d | × λ |
| **per m²** | ÷ (ρ·d) | ÷ d | 1 | × λ/d  (= ÷ R) |
| **per m² R=1** | ÷ (ρ·λ) | ÷ λ | × d/λ  (= × R) | 1 |

---

#### 4. Why the R = 1 basis exists

Comparing insulants per m² or per m³ compares *quantities of material*, not *what
the material does*. 100 mm of mineral wool and 100 mm of PIR occupy the same m², but
do not deliver the same thermal resistance.

The R = 1 basis removes thickness from the comparison. Since **R = d / λ**, the
thickness that delivers R = 1 m²K/W is:

$$d_{R=1} = \lambda \cdot 1 = \lambda \quad [\mathrm{m}]$$

so the material volume behind 1 m² at R = 1 is numerically **λ m³**, and therefore:

$$\text{GWP}_{m^2R=1} = \text{GWP}_{m^3} \cdot \lambda$$

A lower λ means less material is needed for the same performance, and the R = 1
figure rewards that automatically. This is the basis the insulation charts default to.

---

#### 5. Input data and fallback chains

| Symbol | Property | Primary column | Fallback / derivation | Unit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ρ (rho) | Bulk density | `P__Mass_kgm3` | `E__EPD_Density` | kg/m³ |
| d | Thickness | `P__Thick_mm` | `E__EPD_Thick_mm` | mm → m (÷ 1000) |
| λ | Thermal conductivity | `P__L_WmK` | `E__L_WmK` | W/(m·K) |
| m_A | Mass per area | `P__Mass_kgm2` | ρ · d | kg/m² |
| R | Thermal resistance | `E__Rvalue` | d / λ | m²K/W |

The `P__` columns hold the curated library value; the `E__` columns hold what the EPD
itself declared. `P__` wins when both are present, so a conversion always uses the
figure the library has vetted. ρ, d and m_A are over-determined (`m_A = ρ · d`) — a
row where the three disagree signals a data error, not a conversion error.

---

#### 6. Worked example

**Blocco THERMO 450 – 240 mm** — a real catalogue row, declared per m³:

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| `G__GWP_FU` | `m3` |
| `G__GWP_A1A3` | 39.8 kg CO₂e |
| `P__Mass_kgm3` (ρ) | 450 kg/m³ |
| `P__Thick_mm` (d) | 240 mm → 0.240 m |
| `P__L_WmK` (λ) | 0.108 W/(m·K) |

$$\text{GWP}_{m^3} = 39.8 \quad \text{(declared unit is } m^3,\ \text{anchored 1:1)}$$

$$\text{GWP}_{kg} = \frac{39.8}{450} = 0.08844 \;\; \mathrm{kgCO_2e/kg}$$

$$\text{GWP}_{m^2} = 39.8 \times 0.240 = 9.552 \;\; \mathrm{kgCO_2e/m^2}$$

$$\text{GWP}_{m^2R=1} = 39.8 \times 0.108 = 4.2984 \;\; \mathrm{kgCO_2e/m^2\cdot(m^2K/W)}$$

Cross-check: R = 0.240 / 0.108 = 2.222 m²K/W, and 9.552 / 2.222 = 4.298 — the same
figure reached from the m² basis.

---

#### 7. Validity and caveats

- **`_m2R1` is meaningful for insulants only.** It is populated for a few
  non-insulation rows, but λ-normalisation has no functional meaning there.
  `aux_02__chart_value_defaults.json` restricts the column to the *Insulation* product
  type for exactly this reason.
- **`_m2` is thickness-specific.** Two rows of the same product at different
  thicknesses are not comparable on this basis — use `_m3` or `_m2R1`.
- **`_kg` ignores performance and geometry.** It answers "how carbon-intensive is
  this material?", never "how much carbon does this build-up cost?".
- **Linear (`m`) and piece (`unit`) declarations cannot be normalised** without a
  cross-section or a pieces-per-m² figure; those rows stay blank by design.
- **A conversion is only as good as its input.** A missing or wrong ρ, d or λ
  propagates silently into every derived basis.
- **Module scope is A1–A3 throughout.** A4–A5, B, C and D are never folded into
  these columns.

---

#### 8. Where the conversions happen

| Stage | Location | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Source of truth | `EETRA_MaterialLibrary.xlsx` (sheet `_live_data`) | The `_kg` / `_m3` / `_m2` / `_m2R1` columns are computed upstream and stored. The app **reads** them. |
| Ingestion | `04_tools/03_excel_to_parquet.py` | Writes `01_data/base_data.parquet`, preserving the stored conversions unchanged. |
| Data entry | `pages/13_Add_Edit_Item.py` (GWP Data tab) | Re-derives all four bases from the form's own ρ / d / λ and flags any stored value that disagrees by more than ±2%. Read-only — never written back. |
| EPD variants | `libs/lib_epd_family.py`, `pages/13_Add_Edit_Item.py` | **Written.** Products flagged N in an EPD family get reference × factor, with the four bases re-derived by the same rules — see §9. |
| Display fallbacks | `libs/lib_ui.py` (product card) | Fills gaps at render time only: tonne → kg (÷ 1000), and `_m2 ÷ P__Mass_kgm2` → per kg. Not written back. |
| Charts | `libs/lib_charts.py`, `aux_02__chart_value_defaults.json` | Picks the correct basis per product type and hides bases that would mislead. |
| Export | `libs/lib_revalu_send.py`, `libs/lib_revalu_map.py` | `G__GWP_A1A3_kg` maps to Revalu `gwp.a1a3`; ρ, d and λ travel with it so the receiver can re-derive the rest. |

To change a conversion of an ordinary product, edit the source workbook and re-ingest —
editing the app will not alter its stored value. EPD variants (§9) are the exception.

---

#### 9. EPD families — reference product × multiplication factor

Many EPDs publish results for one **reference product** plus a table of factors for
the other products they cover (other thicknesses, facings). Two columns model this:

| Column | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `E__EPD_ConvFactor` | `Y` | Reference product: its GWP data are the figures printed in the EPD (factor 1). |
| `E__EPD_ConvFactor` | `N` | Variant: its GWP data are the reference's × `E__EPD_MultFactor`. |

A family is every product with the same `E__EPD_RegNumber`, compared without
whitespace or case (`S-P- 01137` = `S-P-01137`). For a variant:

- `G__GWP_A1A3` and **every module** A1 … D are multiplied by the factor; non-numeric
  entries (`mnd`, `n/r`) are copied as they are.
- `G__GWP_Metric` and `G__GWP_FU` are copied from the reference.
- The four bases are re-derived (§2–§3) from the scaled A1–A3 and the variant's **own**
  ρ, d and λ. A basis those inputs cannot reach keeps its stored value rescaled by the
  change in A1–A3, so it never goes stale.

In the Add/Edit form a variant's GWP fields are filled in and locked; saving the
reference product rewrites every variant of its family in the same save (the GWP Data
tab previews which ones). Nothing is derived when the family has no product flagged Y,
more than one, or the variant has no numeric factor — the form says which.

The Excel workbook scaled only `G__GWP_A1A3` and copied A4–D unchanged; the app scales
every module, so variants differ from the workbook there after their reference is saved.

## 15. Remote asset storage (Cloudflare R2)

*Embedded from `REMOTE_ASSET_STORAGE.md` — kept as a separate file because it is an operational runbook, followed outside the app when setting up the bucket or re-running the upload. Edit the source file, not this section.*

### Remote asset storage — EPD documents and product images

Updated 2026-10-28. Covers the Cloudflare R2 bucket that backs `01_data/pdf`
(EPD / technical-sheet documents) and `01_data/img` (product-image originals).
Read path: `libs/lib_doc_storage.py`. Upload path:
`04_tools/07_upload_pdfs_to_buckets.py`. Credentials: `.streamlit/secrets.toml`.

**Current state: built, not switched on.** The code is in place and inert;
`[doc_storage] enabled` is `false` and the `[cloudflare_r2]` credentials are
still placeholders. Nothing has been uploaded. Follow *Setup* below to finish.

#### Why

The app carries 1.28 GB of assets that are not code and not data:

| Folder | Files | Size | What it is |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `01_data/pdf` | 905 | 1,232 MB | EPDs, VOC certificates, technical sheets. 888 `.pdf`, 16 `.htm`/`.html`/`.php` saved from manufacturer pages, 1 `.jpg` |
| `01_data/img` | 552 | 51.5 MB | Pipeline-downloaded product-image originals, `sha256(source_url)[:16].<ext>` |

Three consequences, all of which the bucket removes:

1. **A full copy of the PDFs exists twice on disk.** `static/docs` holds 650 of
   them (704 MB) so the catalogue's `srcdoc` iframe can fetch them over plain
   HTTP. The module docstring in `lib_doc_storage.py` says these are hard links
   and "cost no extra disk" — on the OneDrive volume this project lives on, the
   hard-link call falls back to copying, so they are real duplicate bytes.
   Verified with `fsutil hardlink list`, which returns a single path per file.
2. **Streamlit's static folder has a hard 1 GiB cap**, checked once at server
   startup. Go over it and static serving is silently disabled app-wide for the
   life of the process. `MAX_STATIC_DOCS_BYTES` (700 MiB) exists only to stay
   under that ceiling, which is why `static/docs` holds 650 files and not 905 —
   the remaining 255 fall back to a slower server-side fetch.
3. **Product images depend on manufacturer URLs staying put.** When a local
   original is missing the app re-fetches from the source site, so a
   manufacturer reorganising its CDN costs us the picture permanently.

#### Provider

Cloudflare R2, alone. `provider_order = ["cloudflare_r2"]`.

| | Free storage | Egress | Cost for 1.28 GB |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cloudflare R2** | 10 GB, then $0.015/GB-mo | **$0, always** | **$0/mo** |
| Backblaze B2 | 10 GB, then $0.006/GB-mo | free to 3× stored | $0/mo |
| Supabase Storage | 1 GB | 5 GB free | does not fit free → $25/mo Pro |
| AWS S3 | — ($0.023/GB-mo) | $0.09/GB | storage trivial, egress scales badly |

Egress decides it. These are 1.4 MB documents served to browsers, so a
per-GB egress charge is the dominant term everywhere except R2, and Supabase's
free tier cannot hold the PDFs at all. At ten times the current volume R2 is
still about $0.04/month.

The `[supabase]` block stays in `secrets.toml` and the code path still works —
`provider_order` accepts a list and tries each in turn — so a second provider
can be added later without code changes.

#### Bucket layout

One bucket (`eetra-mat-lib`, Western Europe/WEUR) holds both asset classes:

| Key | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<filename>` | `01_data/pdf/<filename>` | Flat, same name as on disk |
| `img/<filename>` | `01_data/img/<filename>` | `img/` prefix |
| `img/_index.json` | generated | `{sha256(url)[:16]: filename}` for every image |

Keys keep their local filenames so the bucket mirrors the folders 1:1 and one
lookup key works for both.

##### Why `img/_index.json` exists

The app knows an image by `sha256(source_url)[:16]`. That hash carries no file
extension, and the folder holds `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.png`, `.webp` and `.gif`.
Resolving a key by probing would be up to five HTTP round trips per miss, and
on a checkout with no `01_data/img` *every* image misses. The index turns all
of that into one cached fetch. A key the index does not list still falls back
to probing, so an object uploaded by hand is still found, just more slowly.

The index is rewritten from the local folder on every run that touches images.
It is uploaded with `max-age=3600`, unlike the assets themselves, so a newly
added image becomes resolvable within the hour.

#### Setup

Four steps in the Cloudflare dashboard, then two commands.

1. **R2 → Create bucket**. The live bucket is `eetra-mat-lib` in Western Europe
   (WEUR); `bucket` in `secrets.toml` must match the name exactly, or every
   `head_object` fails against a bucket that does not exist. The account id in
   the S3 endpoint (`https://<account_id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com/<bucket>`)
   is `38f77d02a49dc885ae5510e665692c31`.
2. **Bucket → Settings → Public access**: enable the `r2.dev` subdomain, or
   bind a custom domain such as `assets.eetra.it`. The app reads over plain
   public HTTPS with no signing, so the bucket must be public-read.
3. **R2 → Manage API Tokens → Create**, with *Object Read & Write* on that
   bucket. Copy the Access Key ID and Secret Access Key — the secret is shown
   once.
4. Fill in `[cloudflare_r2]` in `.streamlit/secrets.toml`: `account_id`,
   `bucket`, `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, `public_base_url`.

Then, from the app root:

```
python 04_tools/07_upload_pdfs_to_buckets.py --target r2 --what both --dry-run
python 04_tools/07_upload_pdfs_to_buckets.py --target r2 --what both
```

Finally set `[doc_storage] enabled = true`.

The upload is ~1.28 GB across 1,456 objects. R2 does not charge for ingress.
Existing objects are skipped via `head_object`, so the run is idempotent and
safe to interrupt and resume; `--force` re-uploads anyway.

The credentials above are used **only** by this offline script. The app never
reads them — it only ever builds a public URL from `public_base_url`.

#### How the app reads it

Documents and images use deliberately different tier orders.

**Documents — remote first** (`fn_fetch_document_bytes`):

> bucket (each provider in `provider_order`) → `01_data/pdf` on disk

A document is fetched once, on demand, when the user opens the document panel.
Remote-first costs nothing there and is what makes the local folder optional.

**Images — remote second** (`fn110_cached_fetch_image` in `libs/lib_data.py`):

> `01_data/img` → product-name local file → `img_manifest.csv` →
> `static/img_cache` → **bucket** → live fetch from the manufacturer

An image is read on every catalogue render and the originals are already on
disk, so the local tiers win and the bucket sits between them and the live
fetch. That ordering is what makes the bucket a link-rot backstop: a hit means
the picture survived either a checkout with no image folder or a source URL
that has since rotted, and nothing gets slower while the local folder is intact.

Both paths are inert while `[doc_storage] enabled` is `false`:
`fn_fetch_image_bytes` returns `(None, None)` and `fetch_remote_image_original`
returns `None`, so the app behaves exactly as it did before.

`fetch_remote_image_original` imports `lib_doc_storage` *inside the function*.
That is deliberate — `lib_doc_storage` imports `_dir_has_file` from `lib_data`,
so a module-level import would close the cycle.

#### Cache-Control

Assets upload with `public, max-age=604800` (7 days). Override with
`--cache-seconds`.

Not the year-long `immutable` that content-addressed assets usually get,
because **these keys are not content hashes**. An image key is the hash of its
*source URL*; a document key is its registration number. Re-issue an EPD under
the same registration, or let a manufacturer swap the picture behind a stable
URL, and the key is unchanged while the bytes are not. A year of `immutable`
would pin the stale copy at every edge with no way to flush it. Seven days
still serves almost every view from cache at no cost.

#### Content types

Every object gets the type its extension implies, via `mimetypes` plus an
explicit table for the cases `mimetypes` gets wrong or does not know
(`.php` → `text/html`, `.webp` → `image/webp`).

This matters because `01_data/pdf` is not all PDFs: 16 of the 905 files are
technical sheets that the manufacturer served as HTML, or `.php` endpoints that
returned a document. Serving those as `application/pdf` makes the browser
download a file it cannot open.

Observed across both folders: 888 `application/pdf`, 393 `image/jpeg`,
86 `image/webp`, 73 `image/png`, 16 `text/html`.

#### Operational notes

- **New assets.** Re-run the uploader after a pipeline run. Existing objects
  are skipped, so a routine run only transfers what is new. Re-run with
  `--what images` after adding images so `img/_index.json` is rewritten.
- **One file is excluded on purpose.** `01_data/img/7ed83ddbe52fe2ab.aspx`
  begins `<!DOCTYP` — it is a saved HTML error page from a failed fetch, not an
  image. The uploader's extension allowlist filters it out.
- **`static/docs` can be retired once this is live.** With documents served
  from R2, `fn_sync_static_doc_links()` and its hourly re-link job
  (`libs/lib_ui.py`) become dead code, and the 704 MB duplicate plus the whole
  Streamlit 1 GiB-cap workaround go with them. Decide first whether
  `01_data/pdf` stays the local master or R2 becomes the master — that choice
  is what makes the local copy droppable.
- **The bucket is public.** Appropriate for published EPD certificates, which
  are already public documents on registry sites such as epditaly.it. Anything
  that should not be public needs presigned URLs instead, which this read path
  does not implement.

#### Metadata

The bucket stores bytes only. `01_data/pdf_manifest.csv` (902 rows) remains the
index — filename, declared/detected type, confidence, `eetra_ids`,
`product_names`, `manufacturers`, `origin_urls`.

If that index ever needs to be queryable or writable by more than one user, it
belongs in the Neon Postgres instance the app already uses for the edit log
(`libs/lib_neon.py`, `psycopg` in `requirements.txt`) — not in the bucket, and
not as blobs in Postgres, where storage costs far more than R2 and CDN caching
is lost entirely.
